text.slice: Automated OriginOS Port

This guide describes the process of creating a port using the auto-script. The port is built on the basis of two firmware packages: the donor (OriginOS — the shell itself) and the stock firmware of the phone to which the port is being transferred.
Step 1. Preparing and Unpacking Firmware
Unpack the payload.bin of both firmware packages. For the auto-script to work correctly, the project folders must be named strictly in a certain way:
Name the stock firmware project "stok" MANDATORILY
Name the donor project (OriginOS) "port" MANDATORILY
From the donor (into the port folder), extract the following partitions:
system, system_ext, product, dyn.img, oem.img, vgc.img
From the stock firmware (into the stok folder), extract only:
system_ext
Don't forget to unpack the img/br files before running the script on both projects
Step 2. Running the Auto-script
After unpacking, run the main auto-port script in the Auto Ports menu, it will notify you when the port is finished
Step 3. Proper Building
After the script has successfully completed, you can proceed to building the images.
It is recommended to build images in erofs, raw format.
Build from the donor folder (port):
system, product, system_ext
Build from the stock folder (stok):
vendor, odm, all **_dlkm (if present)
Step 4. Troubleshooting First Boot (bootloop)
If the device does not boot after building and flashing (bootloop):
Try forcibly replacing the apex files in port/system_ext/apex/ with versions from the stok folder.
After these actions, the firmware should boot.
If the device still does not boot — try changing the OriginOS donor.
